en: The Second Part of the Bhikkhu-vibhaṅga.
Regarding offenses conditioned by engaging in sexual intercourse, by how many of the seven methods of settling are they settled?
Offenses conditioned by engaging in sexual intercourse are settled by three of the seven methods of settling.
It may be settled by both *sammukhāvinaya* and *paṭiññātakaraṇa*;

it may be settled by both *sammukhāvinaya* and *tiṇavatthāraka* … [and so on] … Regarding the offense committed due to showing disrespect by voiding excrement, urine, or spittle into water: by how many of the seven principles for settling disputes is it settled?
In dependence on disrespect, for the purpose of discharging feces, urine, or spittle into water, an offense is settled by three of the seven principles for settling disputes:
it may be settled by face-to-face resolution and by acting according to what has been admitted; or it may be settled by face-to-face resolution and by covering over as with grass.
The seventh section on settling disputes is finished.
